claim: MIN6 pancreatic β cells are very susceptible to ER stress.
source: We have previously shown that the insulin-producing mouse pancreatic β cells MIN6, known for their high metabolic activity, are very susceptible to ER stress (Guan et al., 2014; Krokowski et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Guan et al., 2014; Krokowski et al., 2013).

claim: Upon thapsigargin treatment, MIN6 cells exhibited higher levels of intracellular ROS.
source: Upon Tg treatment, MIN6 cells exhibited higher levels of intracellular ROS, decreased GSH/GSSG (reduced/oxidized glutathione ratios), and increased CTH protein levels via transcriptional activation (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D and supplementary figures.

claim: Upon thapsigargin treatment, MIN6 cells exhibited decreased GSH/GSSG ratios.
source: Upon Tg treatment, MIN6 cells exhibited higher levels of intracellular ROS, decreased GSH/GSSG (reduced/oxidized glutathione ratios), and increased CTH protein levels via transcriptional activation (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D and supplementary figures.

claim: Upon thapsigargin treatment, MIN6 cells exhibited increased CTH protein levels via transcriptional activation.
source: Upon Tg treatment, MIN6 cells exhibited higher levels of intracellular ROS, decreased GSH/GSSG (reduced/oxidized glutathione ratios), and increased CTH protein levels via transcriptional activation (Figure 1B–D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D and supplementary figures.

claim: Transcriptional reprogramming of CTH was observed in mouse and human islets subjected to physiological or pharmacologically induced ER stress.
source: This transcriptional reprogramming was also seen in mouse and human islets subjected to physiological or pharmacologically induced ER stress (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, C and 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and supplementary figures.

claim: H2S levels increased during the chronic phase of the stress response in MIN6 cells.
source: In agreement with increased CTH expression, H2S levels increased during the chronic phase of the stress response (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Expression of the gene encoding the glutamate/cystine exchanger, Slc7a11, was increased during ER stress.
source: Coordinated induction of expression of the gene encoding the glutamate/cystine exchanger, Slc7a11, also was increased (Figure 1D), and this induction was associated with increased glutamate/cystine flux (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and supplementary figure 4.

claim: Increased Slc7a11 expression was associated with increased glutamate/cystine flux.
source: Coordinated induction of expression of the gene encoding the glutamate/cystine exchanger, Slc7a11, also was increased (Figure 1D), and this induction was associated with increased glutamate/cystine flux (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Slc7a11 mediates the exchange of oxidized extracellular cystine with intracellular glutamate.
source: Slc7a11 mediates the exchange of oxidized extracellular cystine with intracellular glutamate.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the function of Slc7a11.

claim: Once cystine is imported into cells it gets reduced to cysteine, and then serves as a substrate for GSH and H2S synthesis.
source: Once cystine is imported into the cells it gets reduced to cysteine, and then serves as a substrate for GSH and H2S synthesis.
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Both increased uptake of the CTH substrate and increased levels of CTH contribute to increased H2S levels in cells under ER stress.
source: These data support the idea that both increased uptake of the CTH substrate and increased levels of CTH contribute to increased H2S levels in cells under ER stress.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on Slc7a11 and CTH expression.

claim: The catalytic activity of GAPDH gradually increased in response to elevated H2S production in MIN6 cells during ER stress.
source: The functional significance of increased H2S synthesis was shown by measuring the catalytic activity of GAPDH (Mustafa et al., 2009), which gradually increased in response to elevated H2S production in MIN6 cells during ER stress (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and cited work (Mustafa et al., 2009).

claim: The increase in GAPDH activity during ER stress was independent of GAPDH protein levels.
source: This increase in activity was independent of GAPDH protein levels (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: GAPDH is catalytically inactive when Cys150 is oxidatively modified, except when it undergoes sulfhydration which restores/increases its activity.
source: As noted above, GAPDH has the unusual feature of being catalytically inactive when Cys150 is oxidatively modified, except when it undergoes sulfhydration which restores/increases its activity (Mustafa et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Mustafa et al., 2009).

claim: The inhibition of GAPDH activity by H2O2 was significantly reversed by H2S treatment in vitro.
source: The inhibition of GAPDH activity by H2O2 was significantly reversed by H2S treatment (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Incubation of purified GAPDH with oxidized glutathione (GSSG) resulted in formation of inactive glutathionylated GAPDH.
source: Furthermore, incubation of purified GAPDH with oxidized glutathione (GSSG) resulted in formation of inactive glutathionylated GAPDH (Gao et al., 2010), which was significantly rescued by treatment with H2S as well as DTT reduction (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H and cited work (Gao et al., 2010).

claim: Glutathionylated GAPDH was significantly rescued by treatment with H2S as well as DTT reduction.
source: Furthermore, incubation of purified GAPDH with oxidized glutathione (GSSG) resulted in formation of inactive glutathionylated GAPDH (Gao et al., 2010), which was significantly rescued by treatment with H2S as well as DTT reduction (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: HPLC-MS confirmed that recombinant GAPDH exposed to NaHS or GSSG was modified predominantly at Cys150.
source: HPLC-MS confirmed that recombinant GAPDH exposed to NaHS or GSSG was modified predominantly at Cys150 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5, Figure 2—figure supplement 7B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: H2S is a positive regulator of GAPDH activity.
source: These data confirm that H2S is a positive regulator of GAPDH activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on GAPDH activity.

claim: Increased GAPDH activity is directly linked to H2S production.
source: Increased GAPDH activity is directly linked to H2S production, as shown by the loss of induction (Figure 1I) upon treatment with the CTH inhibitor, propargylglycine (PAG).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I using the CTH inhibitor PAG.

claim: PAG inhibits H2S synthesis.
source: PAG inhibits H2S synthesis and therefore is expected to decrease Cys150 modification.
evidence: This is a statement of the known mechanism of action of PAG.

claim: Regulation of H2S synthesis during ER stress might regulate the catalytic activity of other metabolic pathway proteins.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that regulation of H2S synthesis during ER stress might regulate the catalytic activity of other metabolic pathway proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the GAPDH data.

claim: ATF4-mediated sulfhydration of proteins is part of the integrated stress response (ISR).
source: The latter is raising the possibility that the ATF4-mediated sulfhydration of proteins is part of the integrated stress response (ISR), and has regulatory effects on cellular metabolism.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: ATF4 increases gene expression of CTH.
source: ATF4 increases gene expression of CTH (Dickhout et al., 2012), the cystine transporter Slc7a11, as well as the ROS-producing enzyme Ero1α (Han et al., 2013; Tabas and Ron, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Dickhout et al., 2012).

claim: ATF4 increases gene expression of the cystine transporter Slc7a11.
source: ATF4 increases gene expression of CTH (Dickhout et al., 2012), the cystine transporter Slc7a11, as well as the ROS-producing enzyme Ero1α (Han et al., 2013; Tabas and Ron, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by the context of ATF4 target genes.

claim: ATF4 increases gene expression of the ROS-producing enzyme Ero1α.
source: ATF4 increases gene expression of CTH (Dickhout et al., 2012), the cystine transporter Slc7a11, as well as the ROS-producing enzyme Ero1α (Han et al., 2013; Tabas and Ron, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Han et al., 2013; Tabas and Ron, 2011).

claim: During ER stress, the network of ATF4 target genes promotes protein sulfhydration.
source: We hypothesized that during ER stress, this network of ATF4 target genes promotes protein sulfhydration (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a hypothesis illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: Knockdown of ATF4 in MIN6 cells during Tg-induced ER stress caused inhibition of H2S synthesis.
source: Knockdown of ATF4 in MIN6 cells during Tg-induced ER stress caused inhibition of H2S synthesis with a parallel loss of induction of CTH protein levels (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Knockdown of ATF4 in MIN6 cells during Tg-induced ER stress caused a parallel loss of induction of CTH protein levels.
source: Knockdown of ATF4 in MIN6 cells during Tg-induced ER stress caused inhibition of H2S synthesis with a parallel loss of induction of CTH protein levels (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In the absence of stress, ATF4 overexpression increased CTH and Ero1α levels.
source: In contrast, in the absence of stress, ATF4 overexpression increased CTH and Ero1α levels and H2S synthesis, in agreement with increased GAPDH activity (Figure 2C–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-E and supplementary figure 1.

claim: In the absence of stress, ATF4 overexpression increased H2S synthesis.
source: In contrast, in the absence of stress, ATF4 overexpression increased CTH and Ero1α levels and H2S synthesis, in agreement with increased GAPDH activity (Figure 2C–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-E.

claim: In the absence of stress, ATF4 overexpression increased GAPDH activity.
source: In contrast, in the absence of stress, ATF4 overexpression increased CTH and Ero1α levels and H2S synthesis, in agreement with increased GAPDH activity (Figure 2C–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-E.

claim: The levels of GSH increased with ATF4 overexpression.
source: The levels of GSH and the activity of the glutamate/cystine exchanger also increased with ATF4 overexpression (Figure 2F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The activity of the glutamate/cystine exchanger increased with ATF4 overexpression.
source: The levels of GSH and the activity of the glutamate/cystine exchanger also increased with ATF4 overexpression (Figure 2F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: ATF4 is a master regulator of protein sulfhydration in pancreatic β cells during ER stress.
source: These data support the hypothesis that ATF4 is a master regulator of protein sulfhydration in pancreatic β cells during ER stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ATF4 manipulation.

claim: The BTA approach allows quantitative assessment of changes in the sulfhydration of specific cysteines in the proteome.
source: In this study, we introduced the BTA approach that allowed the quantitative assessment of changes in the sulfhydration of specific cysteines in the proteome and in individual proteins.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of the developed method.

claim: BTA is superior to other reported methodologies that aimed to profile cysteine modifications, such as the modified biotin switch technique (BST).
source: BTA is superior to other reported methodologies that aimed to profile cysteine modifications, such as the most commonly used, a modified biotin switch technique (BST).
evidence: This is a comparative claim about the BTA method.

claim: BST was originally designed to study protein nitrosylation and postulated to differentiate free thiols and persulfides.
source: BST was originally designed to study protein nitrosylation and postulated to differentiate free thiols and persulfides (Mustafa et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Mustafa et al., 2009).

claim: A key advantage of BTA over existing methodologies is that the experimental approach has steps to avoid false-positive and negative results.
source: A key advantage of BTA over the existing methodologies is that the experimental approach has steps to avoid false-positive and negative results, as target proteins for sulfhydration.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the BTA method.

claim: BST is commonly generating false targets for cysteine modifications.
source: BST is commonly generating such false targets for cysteine modifications (Forrester et al., 2009; Sen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Forrester et al., 2009; Sen et al., 2012).

claim: Almost 1000 sulfhydrated cysteine-containing peptides were present in MIN6 cells under chronic ER stress condition of treatment with Tg for 18 hr.
source: Almost 1000 sulfhydrated cysteine-containing peptides were present in the cells under the chronic ER stress condition of treatment with Tg for 18 hr.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the BTA analysis.

claim: Almost 820 peptides on more than 500 proteins were quantified in MIN6 cells overexpressing ATF4.
source: Combined with the isotopic-labeling strategy, almost 820 peptides on more than 500 proteins were quantified in the cells overexpressing ATF4.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the BTA analysis with isotopic labeling.

claim: The current dataset encompasses most known sulfhydrated cysteine residues in proteins in any organism.
source: To our knowledge, the current dataset encompasses most known sulfhydrated cysteine residues in proteins in any organism.
evidence: This is a claim about the comprehensiveness of the dataset.

claim: An arginine residue and alpha-helix dipoles both contribute to stabilize sulfhydrated cysteine thiolates in the local environment.
source: Structure and sequence analysis revealed consensus motifs that favor sulfhydration; an arginine residue and alpha-helix dipoles are both contributing to stabilize sulfhydrated cysteine thiolates in the local environment.
evidence: This is a conclusion from bioinformatics analysis of the sulfhydrated peptides.

claim: H2S-mediated sulfhydration of cysteine residues is part of the ISR with the highest enrichment in proteins involved in energy metabolism.
source: Pathway analyses showed that H2S-mediated sulfhydration of cysteine residues is the part of the ISR with the highest enrichment in proteins involved in energy metabolism.
evidence: This is a conclusion from pathway analysis of the sulfhydrated proteins.

claim: H2S promotes aerobic glycolysis associated with decreased oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria during ER stress in β cells.
source: The metabolic flux revealed that H2S promotes aerobic glycolysis associated with decreased oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria during ER stress in β cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion from metabolic flux analysis.

claim: Pyruvate carboxylase was found to be sulfhydrated.
source: This latter enzyme was found to be sulfhydrated, consistent with the notion that sulfhydration is linked to metabolic reprogramming toward glycolysis.
evidence: This is a finding from the BTA analysis.

claim: The switch of energy production from mitochondria to glycolysis is known as a signature of hypoxic conditions.
source: The switch of energy production from mitochondria to glycolysis is known as a signature of hypoxic conditions.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge.

claim: The metabolic switch from mitochondria to glycolysis has been observed in many cancer cells characterized as the Warburg effect.
source: This metabolic switch has also been observed in many cancer cells characterized as the Warburg effect, which contributes to tumor growth.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about cancer metabolism.

claim: The Warburg effect provides advantages to cancer cell survival via rapid ATP production through glycolysis.
source: The Warburg effect provides advantages to cancer cell survival via the rapid ATP production through glycolysis, as well as the increasd conversion of glucose into anabolic biomolecules (amino acid, nucleic acid, and lipid biosynthesis) and reducing power (NADPH) for regeneration of antioxidants.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the Warburg effect.

claim: The Warburg effect provides advantages to cancer cell survival via increased conversion of glucose into anabolic biomolecules and reducing power (NADPH) for regeneration of antioxidants.
source: The Warburg effect provides advantages to cancer cell survival via the rapid ATP production through glycolysis, as well as the increasd conversion of glucose into anabolic biomolecules (amino acid, nucleic acid, and lipid biosynthesis) and reducing power (NADPH) for regeneration of antioxidants.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the Warburg effect.

claim: The metabolic response of tumor cells contributes to tumor growth and metastasis.
source: This metabolic response of tumor cells contributes to tumor growth and metastasis (Vander Heiden et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Vander Heiden et al., 2009).

claim: The aerobic glycolysis triggered by increased H2S production could give β cells the capability to acquire ATP and nutrients to adapt their cellular metabolism toward maintaining ATP levels in the ER.
source: By analogy, the aerobic glycolysis trigged by increased H2S production could give β cells the capability to acquire ATP and nutrients to adapt their cellular metabolism toward maintaining ATP levels in the ER (Vishnu et al., 2014), increasing synthesis of glycerolphospholipids, glycoproteins and protein (Krokowski et al., 2013), all important components of the ISR.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on analogy to the Warburg effect, supported by citations (Vishnu et al., 2014; Krokowski et al., 2013).

claim: The decreased mitochondria function in β cells during ER stress can be viewed as an adaptive response by limiting mitochondria ROS and mitochondria-mediated apoptosis.
source: Similar to hypoxic conditions, a phenotype associated with most tumors, the decreased mitochondria function in β cells during ER stress, can also be viewed as an adaptive response by limiting mitochondria ROS and mitochondria-mediated apoptosis.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the metabolic changes.

claim: The H2S-mediated increase in glycolysis is an adaptive mechanism for survival of β cells to chronic ER stress.
source: We therefore view that the H2S-mediated increase in glycolysis is an adaptive mechanism for survival of β cells to chronic ER stress, along with the improved ER function and insulin production and folding, both critical factors controlling hyperglycemia in diabetes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Abnormal H2S metabolism has been reported to occur in various diseases, mostly through the deregulation of gene expression encoding for H2S-generating enzymes.
source: Abnormal H2S metabolism has been reported to occur in various diseases, mostly through the deregulation of gene expression encoding for H2S-generating enzymes (Wallace and Wang, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Wallace and Wang, 2015).

claim: ER stress in β cells induced elevated CTH levels, whereas CBS was unaffected.
source: In the present study, ER stress in β cells induced elevated CTH levels, whereas CBS was unaffected.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: The deregulated oxidative modification at cysteine residues by H2S may be a major contributing factor to disease development.
source: The deregulated oxidative modification at cysteine residues by H2S may be a major contributing factor to disease development.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: Tg-treatment significantly augmented glycolytic flux as determined by the increase in 3 phosphoglyceric acid (3PG), lactate, and alanine.
source: Tg-treatment significantly augmented glycolytic flux as determined by the increase in the glycolytic intermediate, 3 phosphoglyceric acid (3PG), as well as lactate and alanine (Figure 4A–C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolic flux data shown in Figure 4A-C and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Lactate levels were decreased significantly despite the increased glycolytic flux during Tg treatment.
source: However, lactate levels were decreased significantly despite the increased flux.
evidence: This is a finding from the metabolic flux analysis.

claim: A decrease in cellular lactate levels supports the idea that there is high consumption of pyruvate by the mitochondria to generate oxaloacetate (OAA).
source: A decrease in cellular lactate levels supports the idea that there is high consumption of pyruvate by the mitochondria to generate oxaloacetate (OAA).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lactate data.

claim: Flux to tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) intermediates was significantly reduced by Tg-treatment.
source: In contrast to the increased glycolytic rates, flux to tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) intermediates was significantly reduced by Tg-treatment as evidenced by the low 13C label incorporation of both acetyl-CoA and OAA moieties of citrate, fumarate, and malate (Figure 4A–B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolic flux data shown in Figure 4A-B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: When cells were exposed to PAG along with Tg-treatment, the increase in glycolytic flux was prevented.
source: When the cells were exposed to PAG along with Tg-treatment, the increase in glycolytic flux was prevented, as shown by the decrease in 13C-labeling of 3PG, lactate, and alanine.
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolic flux data with PAG treatment.

claim: TCA cycle flux was restored when cells were exposed to PAG along with Tg-treatment.
source: In contrast, TCA cycle flux was restored, as exemplified by the increase in 13C-labeling of both OAA and acetyl-CoA moieties of citrate, succinate, fumarate, and malate, and a decrease in their concentrations, suggesting utilization.
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolic flux data with PAG treatment.

claim: 13C-labeling of aspartate and glutamine increased significantly when cells were exposed to PAG along with Tg-treatment.
source: 13C-labeling of aspartate and glutamine also increased significantly, indicating increased cataplerosis of TCA cycle intermediates.
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolic flux data with PAG treatment.

claim: Tg-treatment increased PKM2 activity.
source: Tg-treatment increased PKM2 activity, but PAG addition inhibited the increase, without affecting PKM2 protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: PAG addition inhibited the increase in PKM2 activity during Tg treatment, without affecting PKM2 protein levels.
source: Tg-treatment increased PKM2 activity, but PAG addition inhibited the increase, without affecting PKM2 protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: ER stress, via H2S-mediated signaling, promotes glycolysis and decreases mitochondrial oxidative metabolism.
source: These data suggest that ER stress, via H2S-mediated signaling, promotes glycolysis and decreases mitochondrial oxidative metabolism.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the metabolic flux data.

claim: Over 1000 novel sulfhydrated cysteines in MIN6 cells treated with Tg were identified, corresponding to about 820 proteins.
source: By using the modified BTA technique, we have identified over ~ 1000 novel sulfhydrated cysteines in MIN6 cells treated with Tg, corresponding to about 820 proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 9 and Figure 2—source data 1), including GAPDH, wherein two cysteine-containing peptides were captured: Cys150 and Cys245.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 9 and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: The Cys150 active-site peptide of GAPDH was highly enriched compared to the C-terminal Cys245.
source: Remarkably, the Cys150 active-site peptide was highly enriched as compared to the C-terminal of Cys245, supporting prior mutagenesis studies that have shown Cys150 as the primary H2S-modified site on GAPDH, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is a finding from the BTA analysis that is consistent with prior studies.

claim: Cys150 is the primary H2S-modified site on GAPDH, both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Remarkably, the Cys150 active-site peptide was highly enriched as compared to the C-terminal of Cys245, supporting prior mutagenesis studies that have shown Cys150 as the primary H2S-modified site on GAPDH, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by prior mutagenesis studies and the current BTA data.

claim: PHGDH is a novel target for sulfhydration.
source: One of novel targets including phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) was also confirmed by Western blot analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 10.

claim: CTH knockdown mediated by shRNA decreased GAPDH and PHGDH sulfhydration levels.
source: CTH Knockdown mediated by shRNA decreased GAPDH and PHGDH sulfhydration levels, confirming that those proteins identified by the BTA method are bona-fide targets for sulfhydration in vivo (Figure 2—figure supplement 11).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 11.

claim: Sulfhydrated peptides do not reveal a consensus protein abundance and sulfhydrome.
source: Sulfhydrated peptides do not reveal a consensus protein abundance and sulfhydrome (Figure 3—figure supplement 6,7and Figure 3—source data 2), supporting that lower concentrations of the NM-biotin labeling reveal reactivity of cysteine residues rather than protein abundance.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6, 7 and Figure 3—source data 2.

claim: Lower concentrations of NM-biotin labeling reveal reactivity of cysteine residues rather than protein abundance.
source: Sulfhydrated peptides do not reveal a consensus protein abundance and sulfhydrome (Figure 3—figure supplement 6,7and Figure 3—source data 2), supporting that lower concentrations of the NM-biotin labeling reveal reactivity of cysteine residues rather than protein abundance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of sulfhydrome and protein abundance.

claim: Over 834 cysteine-containing peptides were identified in ATF4-expressing MIN6 cells.
source: Using the experimental plan in Figure 3A, we identified over 834 cysteine-containing peptides (Figure 3B and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: Of 834 cysteine-containing peptides identified, 771 exhibited pair-labeling with an overall average H/L ratio 2.6.
source: Of these peptides, 771 exhibited pair-labeling with an overall average H/L ratio 2.6, and 348 peptides (45%) displayed high ratios (H/L>2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the isotopic labeling experiment.

claim: 348 peptides (45%) displayed high H/L ratios (H/L>2) in ATF4-expressing MIN6 cells.
source: Of these peptides, 771 exhibited pair-labeling with an overall average H/L ratio 2.6, and 348 peptides (45%) displayed high ratios (H/L>2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the isotopic labeling experiment.

claim: ATF4 drives global changes in protein sulfhydration in MIN6 cells.
source: These findings confirmed that ATF4 drives global changes in protein sulfhydration in MIN6 cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative sulfhydrome data.

claim: 28% of the 827 sulfhydrated peptides were localized to protein regions whose structural and functional properties are known.
source: The analysis revealed that 28% of the peptides were localized to protein regions whose structural and functional properties are known (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatics analysis shown in Figure 3C and supplementary figure 1.

claim: An additional 18% of sulfhydrated peptides were found within functional regions of proteins with cysteine residues of unknown significance.
source: An additional 18% were found within functional regions of proteins with cysteine residues of unknown significance.
evidence: This is a result from the bioinformatics analysis.

claim: Sulfhydration of specific cysteine residues within functional domains of proteins suggests that the cysteine modification influences the activity of proteins.
source: Our finding of sulfhydration of specific cysteine residues within functional domains of proteins suggests that the cysteine modification influences the activity of proteins.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the bioinformatics analysis.

claim: 4.2% of the sulfhydrated peptides contained cysteine residues in experimentally proven active sites of enzymes or cysteine residues involved in disulfide bond formation.
source: In contrast, 4.2% of the peptides in question contained cysteine residues in experimentally proven active sites of enzymes or cysteine residues involved in disulfide bond formation (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatics analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The percentage of active cysteine-containing peptides from the BTA assay (4.2%) is significantly larger than the 0.2% of all cysteines in the Uniprot database that have been assigned to experimentally characterized active cysteines.
source: This percentage of active cysteine-containing peptides from the BTA assay is significantly larger than the 0.2% of all cysteines in the Uniprot database that have been assigned to experimentally characterized active cysteines (Weerapana et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparative analysis with the Uniprot database, supported by citation (Weerapana et al., 2010).

claim: 2.4% of the annotated sulfhydrated peptides were found in known nucleotide binding domains of proteins.
source: Finally, 2.4% of the annotated peptides were found in known nucleotide binding domains of proteins, suggesting the potential for regulation of gene expression by H2S cysteine-modified proteins.
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatics analysis.

claim: Sulfhydration of nucleotide binding domains suggests the potential for regulation of gene expression by H2S cysteine-modified proteins.
source: Finally, 2.4% of the annotated peptides were found in known nucleotide binding domains of proteins, suggesting the potential for regulation of gene expression by H2S cysteine-modified proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the location of sulfhydrated cysteines.

claim: The NF-κB RelA transcription factor has been shown to be sulfhydrated in the DNA-binding domain, resulting in increased DNA-binding activity.
source: Although not found among the 827 peptides in this study, the NF-κB RelA transcription factor has been shown to be sulfhydrated in the DNA-binding domain, resulting in increased DNA-binding activity (Sen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Sen et al., 2012).

claim: 11% of the 834 sulfhydrated peptides from the RedoxDB corresponded to cysteine residues that are known to be modified by nitrosylation or glutathionylation.
source: We also found by querying the redox modification databases (RedoxDB and GPS-SNO) that 11% of the 834 peptides from the RedoxDB and 36% from the GPS-SNO corresponded to cysteine residues that are known to be modified by nitrosylation or glutathionylation (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by database query results shown in Figure 3B and supplementary figure 2.

claim: 36% of the 834 sulfhydrated peptides from the GPS-SNO corresponded to cysteine residues that are known to be modified by nitrosylation or glutathionylation.
source: We also found by querying the redox modification databases (RedoxDB and GPS-SNO) that 11% of the 834 peptides from the RedoxDB and 36% from the GPS-SNO corresponded to cysteine residues that are known to be modified by nitrosylation or glutathionylation (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by database query results shown in Figure 3B and supplementary figure 2.

claim: Protein sulfhydration not only influences the catalytic activity of enzymes like GAPDH, but also can potentially regulate a broad range of biological processes.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that protein sulfhydration not only influences the catalytic activity of enzymes like GAPDH, but also can potentially regulate a broad range of biological processes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the bioinformatics analysis of sulfhydrated proteins.

claim: Labeled cysteines on the same protein exhibited remarkably different H/L ratios.
source: In addition, labeled cysteines on the same protein exhibited remarkably different ratios (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: PHGDH was labeled on two cysteines: Cys281 had an H/L ratio of 5.8, whereas Cys254 displayed a ratio of 17.
source: For example, the protein, PHGDH, was labeled on two cysteines, Cys281 had an H/L ratio of 5.8, whereas Cys254 displayed a ratio of 17.
evidence: This is a specific example from the quantitative sulfhydrome data.

claim: Analysis of all cysteine-containing peptides did not reveal conserved residues surrounding the modified cysteine site.
source: This analysis did not reveal conserved residues surrounding the modified cysteine site (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A), a result consistent with other enzyme-independent oxidative modifications of cysteines (Weerapana et al., 2010) (Marino and Gladyshev, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and citations (Weerapana et al., 2010; Marino and Gladyshev, 2011).

claim: When selecting only peptides with high H/L ratios (>2), an Arg residue was significantly enriched at the +1 position of the modified cysteine.
source: However, when we selected only the peptides with high H/L ratios (>2), and searched for a sequence motif at the cysteine modification sites (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B), an Arg residue was significantly enriched at the +1 position of the modified cysteine (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Structure motif and surface accessibility analysis revealed that the modified cysteine is highly accessible and positioned at the N-terminal alpha-helices.
source: Additionally, structure motif and surface accessibility analysis revealed that the modified cysteine is highly accessible and positioned at the N-terminal alpha-helices (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4C-D.

claim: A reactive cysteine thiolate anion is stabilized by interaction with alpha-helix dipoles.
source: This is consistent with previous reports suggesting that a reactive cysteine thiolate anion is stabilized by interaction with alpha-helix dipoles (Kortemme and Creighton, 1995; Weerapana et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Kortemme and Creighton, 1995; Weerapana et al., 2010).

claim: Bioinformatics clustering revealed an enrichment of sulfhydrated proteins in glycolysis and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism.
source: Bioinformatics clustering with two pathway annotation programs DAVID and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) revealed an enrichment of sulfhydrated proteins in glycolysis and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway analysis shown in Figure 3E and supplementary figure 5.

claim: ATF4-overexpressing MIN6 cells had higher glycolytic rates.
source: Also in agreement with this hypothesis, we found that ATF4-overexpressing MIN6 cells had higher glycolytic rates as evaluated with a Seahorse analyzer (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The activity of the rate-limiting glycolytic enzyme, pyruvate kinase 2 (PKM2), was increased in ATF4 overexpressing MIN6 cells, in a manner dependent on CTH activity.
source: Furthermore, the activity of the rate-limiting glycolytic enzyme, pyruvate kinase 2 (PKM2), also was increased in ATF4 overexpressing MIN6 cells, in a manner dependent on CTH activity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Sulfhydration of cysteine residues in proteins is an important mechanism involved in diverse biological processes.
source: The sulfhydration of cysteine residues in proteins is an important mechanism involved in diverse biological processes.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract summarizing the importance of sulfhydration.

claim: Bioinformatics analysis revealed that sulfhydrated cysteines are part of a wide range of biological functions.
source: Bioinformatics analysis revealed that sulfhydrated cysteines are part of a wide range of biological functions.
evidence: This is a summary statement from the abstract about the bioinformatics findings.

claim: In pancreatic β cells exposed to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, elevated H2S promotes the sulfhydration of enzymes in energy metabolism and stimulates glycolytic flux.
source: In pancreatic β cells exposed to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, elevated H2S promotes the sulfhydration of enzymes in energy metabolism and stimulates glycolytic flux.
evidence: This is a summary statement from the abstract about the main findings.

claim: Transcriptional and translational reprogramming by the integrated stress response (ISR) in pancreatic β cells is coupled to metabolic alternations triggered by sulfhydration of key enzymes in intermediary metabolism.
source: We propose that transcriptional and translational reprogramming by the integrated stress response (ISR) in pancreatic β cells is coupled to metabolic alternations triggered by sulfhydration of key enzymes in intermediary metabolism.
evidence: This is the main proposal/hypothesis stated in the abstract.

claim: Reactive cysteine residues in proteins have high nucleophilicity and low pKa values and serve as a major target for oxidative modifications.
source: Reactive cysteine residues in proteins have high nucleophilicity and low pKa values and serve as a major target for oxidative modifications, which can vary depending on the subcellular environment, including the type and intensity of intracellular or environmental cues.
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge.

claim: Oxidative environments cause different post-translational cysteine modifications, including disulfide bond formation, sulfenylation, nitrosylation, glutathionylation, and sulfhydration.
source: Oxidative environments cause different post-translational cysteine modifications, including disulfide bond formation (-S-S-), sulfenylation (-S-OH), nitrosylation (-S-NO), glutathionylation (-S-SG), and sulfhydration (-S-SH) (also called persulfidation) (Finkel, 2012; Mishanina et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge supported by citations (Finkel, 2012; Mishanina et al., 2015).

claim: In sulfhydration, an oxidized cysteine residue on a protein reacts with the sulfide anion to form a cysteine persulfide.
source: In the latter, an oxidized cysteine residue included glutathionylated, sulfenylated, and nitrosylated on a protein reacts with the sulfide anion to form a cysteine persulfide.
evidence: This is a statement of the mechanism of sulfhydration.

claim: The reversible nature of sulfhydration provides a mechanism to fine tune biological processes in different cellular redox states.
source: The reversible nature of this modification provides a mechanism to fine tune biological processes in different cellular redox states.
evidence: This is a statement about the functional significance of sulfhydration reversibility.

claim: Sulfhydration coordinates with other post-translational protein modifications such as phosphorylation and nitrosylation to regulate cellular functions.
source: Sulfhydration coordinates with other post-translational protein modifications such as phosphorylation and nitrosylation to regulate cellular functions (Altaany et al., 2014; Sen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Altaany et al., 2014; Sen et al., 2012).

claim: Identification of different cysteine-based protein modifications has been slow compared to other post-translational modifications.
source: Despite great progress in bioinformatics and advanced mass spectroscopic (MS) techniques, identification of different cysteine-based protein modifications has been slow compared to other post-translational modifications.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: A small number of proteins have been identified as targets for sulfhydration, among them the glycolytic enzyme glyceraldehyde phosphate dehydrogenase, GAPDH.
source: In the case of sulfhydration, a small number of proteins have been identified, among them the glycolytic enzyme glyceraldehyde phosphate dehydrogenase, GAPDH (Mustafa et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Mustafa et al., 2009).

claim: Sulfhydrated GAPDH at Cys150 exhibits an increase in its catalytic activity.
source: Sulfhydrated GAPDH at Cys150 exhibits an increase in its catalytic activity, in contrast to the inhibitory effects of nitrosylation or glutathionylation of the same cysteine residue (Mustafa et al., 2009; Paul and Snyder, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Mustafa et al., 2009; Paul and Snyder, 2012).

claim: Nitrosylation or glutathionylation of Cys150 on GAPDH has inhibitory effects on its catalytic activity.
source: Sulfhydrated GAPDH at Cys150 exhibits an increase in its catalytic activity, in contrast to the inhibitory effects of nitrosylation or glutathionylation of the same cysteine residue (Mustafa et al., 2009; Paul and Snyder, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Mustafa et al., 2009; Paul and Snyder, 2012).

claim: H2S could serve as a biological switch for protein function acting via oxidative modification of specific cysteine residues in response to redox homeostasis.
source: The biological significance of the Cys150 modification by H2S is not well-studied, but H2S could serve as a biological switch for protein function acting via oxidative modification of specific cysteine residues in response to redox homeostasis (Paul and Snyder, 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citation (Paul and Snyder, 2012).

claim: Current methodologies based on the modified biotin switch technique do not allow detection of a broad spectrum of sulfhydrated proteins.
source: Current methodologies based on the modified biotin switch technique do not allow detection of a broad spectrum of sulfhydrated proteins (Finkel, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation (Finkel, 2012).

claim: The ER is an organelle involved in the synthesis of proteins followed by various modifications.
source: The ER is an organelle involved in the synthesis of proteins followed by various modifications.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about ER function.

claim: Disruption of protein synthesis and modification in the ER results in the accumulation of misfolded proteins, causing ER stress.
source: Disruption of this process results in the accumulation of misfolded proteins, causing ER stress (Tabas and Ron, 2011; Walter and Ron, 2011), which is associated with development of many diseases ranging from metabolic dysfunction to neurodegeneration (Hetz, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations (Tabas and Ron, 2011; Walter and Ron, 2011; Hetz, 2012).

claim: ER stress is associated with development of many diseases ranging from metabolic dysfunction to neurodegeneration.
source: Disruption of this process results in the accumulation of misfolded proteins, causing ER stress (Tabas and Ron, 2011; Walter and Ron, 2011), which is associated with development of many diseases ranging from metabolic dysfunction to neurodegeneration (Hetz, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation (Hetz, 2012).

claim: ER stress induces transcriptional, translational, and metabolic reprogramming, all of which are interconnected through the transcription factor ATF4.
source: ER stress induces transcriptional, translational, and metabolic reprogramming, all of which are interconnected through the transcription factor ATF4.
evidence: This is a statement about the role of ATF4 in the ER stress response.

claim: ATF4 increases expression of genes promoting adaptation to stress via their protein products.
source: ATF4 increases expression of genes promoting adaptation to stress via their protein products.
evidence: This is a statement about the function of ATF4.

claim: CTH (cystathionine gamma-lyase or γ-cystathionase) is an H2S-producing enzyme.
source: One such gene is the H2S-producing enzyme, cystathionine gamma-lyase (CTH) or γ-cystathionase , previously shown to be involved in the signaling pathway that negatively regulates the activity of the protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) via sulfhydration (Krishnan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge supported by citation (Krishnan et al., 2011).

claim: CTH was previously shown to be involved in the signaling pathway that negatively regulates the activity of the protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) via sulfhydration.
source: One such gene is the H2S-producing enzyme, cystathionine gamma-lyase (CTH) or γ-cystathionase , previously shown to be involved in the signaling pathway that negatively regulates the activity of the protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) via sulfhydration (Krishnan et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Krishnan et al., 2011).

claim: Low or even modest levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) during ER stress may reprogram cellular metabolism via H2S-mediated protein sulfhydration.
source: We therefore hypothesized that low or even modest levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) during ER stress may reprogram cellular metabolism via H2S-mediated protein sulfhydration (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is the main hypothesis of the study, illustrated in Figure 1A.
